name: Chapter 1 - Computer Architecture
description: Study plan focusing on Chapter 1: Computer Architecture (Introduction) and Chapter 2: Data Representation (Representing Text). This plan adds two new tasks aligned with the provided textbook topics and includes guiding questions and objectives to support understanding.

tasks.name: 1. Computer Architecture - 1.1 Introduction to Computer Architecture
tasks.description: Study the fundamentals of computer architecture, including the purpose of architecture, core components, and factors influencing performance. [Guiding questions and objectives provided below]
guiding_qns: What is the purpose of computer architecture and what are its main components?
How do CPU, memory, and I/O interact in a typical system?
What is the difference between Von Neumann and Harvard architectures?
What drives architectural decisions in terms of performance and energy efficiency?
What is memory hierarchy and why is it important?
objectives: Define computer architecture and identify its major components.
Explain how the CPU, memory, and I/O subsystem interact.
Describe Von Neumann vs Harvard architectures.
Explain the concept of memory hierarchy and its impact on performance.
Identify factors that influence architectural decisions.

tasks.name: 2. Data Representation - 2.4 Representing Text
tasks.description: Explore how text is encoded and stored in computers, including character sets, encodings, and binary representations. [Guiding questions and objectives provided below]
guiding_qns: What are the goals of text encoding in computing?
What is ASCII and what are its limitations?
What is Unicode and why was it created?
What are UTF-8 and UTF-16 encodings and how do they differ?
How do you encode and decode characters in binary form?
What is endianness and how can it affect text representation on different systems?
objectives: Explain the purpose of text encoding and the relationship between characters, code points, and encodings.
Describe ASCII and Unicode standards and their limitations.
Explain UTF-8 and UTF-16 encodings and when each is used.
Demonstrate how to convert text to binary representations and back.
Discuss the concept of endianness and its impact on text data.

comments: New tasks added for study plan; align with textbook topics and provide guiding questions and objectives.
